explain.es: Un idiom es una expresión fija cuyo significado no se deduce de la suma de sus palabras: spill the beans no tiene nada que ver con judías; significa irse de la lengua. En C2 se espera que los reconozcas al instante en la prensa, la literatura y la conversación, y que uses los más frecuentes con naturalidad, respetando su forma exacta y su registro. Algunos coinciden con el español (the tip of the iceberg), muchos usan otra imagen (cost an arm and a leg = costar un ojo de la cara) y otros son auténticas trampas.
explain.en: An idiom is a fixed expression whose meaning cannot be worked out from its individual words. At C2 you should recognise idioms instantly and use the common ones accurately, in their exact form and in the right register.
formula: spill the beans + ≠ + derramar las judías
spill the beans + = + *irse de la lengua*

explain.title: 1 · Bloque fijo, piezas móviles
explain.es: Un idiom es un bloque, pero no está congelado del todo. Lo que cambia: el verbo se conjuga (she threw in the towel), los posesivos concuerdan con el sujeto (I bit my tongue · they pulled their weight) y algunos tienen un hueco para la persona (pull someone's leg → pull my leg). Lo que no cambia: los sustantivos, los artículos, las preposiciones y el número (throw the towel, beat about the bushes). Muy pocos admiten pasiva sin perder el sentido figurado: the hatchet has been buried se oye, pero the bush was beaten about suena absurdo.
explain.en: Verbs change tense, possessives agree with the subject and some idioms have a slot for a person. Nouns, articles, prepositions and number are fixed. Most idioms resist the passive.

examples.en: The consortium finally threw in the towel after its third bid.
examples.es: El consorcio por fin tiró la toalla tras su tercera oferta.

examples.en: She was my boss, so I had to bite my tongue.
examples.es: Era mi jefa, así que tuve que morderme la lengua.
Por fin se ha enterrado el hacha de guerra.

explain.title: 2 · No todos tienen el mismo registro
explain.es: Hay idioms neutros, habituales en la prensa seria y en los informes (a bone of contention, the tip of the iceberg, at the eleventh hour, in the red); idioms coloquiales, propios de la conversación y de la prensa popular (a piece of cake, spill the beans, get the sack), y algunos muy británicos e informales (take the mickey). En un ensayo académico lo más seguro es sustituir el idiom por una paráfrasis.
explain.en: Neutral idioms appear in quality journalism and reports; colloquial ones belong to conversation and the tabloids. In academic writing, paraphrase.

examples.en: Pay remains a bone of contention between unions and management. (prensa)
examples.es: El salario sigue siendo la manzana de la discordia entre sindicatos y dirección.
Las negociaciones fracasaron en el último momento.

examples.en: Honestly, the interview was a piece of cake. (coloquial)
examples.es: La verdad, la entrevista fue pan comido.

examples.en: Are you taking the mickey? (muy coloquial, BrE)

explain.title: Idiomático o formal
explain.es: El mismo contenido en dos registros. En un informe, una carta formal o un ensayo, sustituye el idiom coloquial por un verbo o una expresión neutra.
explain.en: Same content, two registers: in reports and essays, replace colloquial idioms with neutral wording.

explain.title: Trabajo y dinero
head: Idiom · meaning
Español
Ejemplo · Example
rows:
cost an arm and a leg
be extremely expensive
costar un ojo de la cara

Renting in central London costs an arm and a leg.
Alquilar en el centro de Londres cuesta un ojo de la cara.

make ends meet
have just enough money to live on
llegar a fin de mes

Many nurses are struggling to make ends meet.
Muchas enfermeras tienen dificultades para llegar a fin de mes.

tighten your belt
spend less money
apretarse el cinturón

After the merger, every department had to tighten its belt.
Tras la fusión, todos los departamentos tuvieron que apretarse el cinturón.

be in the red
be losing money; be in debt
estar en números rojos

The airline has been in the red since the pandemic.
La aerolínea está en números rojos desde la pandemia.

learn the ropes
learn how a job is done
aprender el oficio, hacerse con el puesto

Give the new analyst a few weeks to learn the ropes.
Dale al nuevo analista unas semanas para hacerse con el puesto.

pull your weight
do your fair share of the work
arrimar el hombro

If one member doesn't pull their weight, the whole team suffers.
Si un miembro no arrima el hombro, todo el equipo lo paga.

get the sack
be dismissed from your job
ser despedido, que te echen

He got the sack for leaking confidential data.
Lo echaron por filtrar datos confidenciales.

a cash cow
a reliable source of profit
la gallina de los huevos de oro

The subscription service has become the firm's cash cow.
Las suscripciones se han convertido en la gallina de los huevos de oro de la empresa.

back to the drawing board
time to start planning again
volver a empezar desde cero

The investors rejected the plan, so it's back to the drawing board.
Los inversores rechazaron el plan, así que toca volver a empezar.

explain.title: Éxito, fracaso y esfuerzo
head: Idiom · meaning
Español
Ejemplo · Example
rows:
hit the nail on the head
describe something exactly right
dar en el clavo

Your analysis hit the nail on the head.
Tu análisis dio en el clavo.

a piece of cake
something very easy
pan comido, coser y cantar

After all that revision, the exam was a piece of cake.
Después de tanto repasar, el examen fue pan comido.

throw in the towel
give up
tirar la toalla

After three failed bids, the consortium threw in the towel.
Tras tres ofertas fallidas, el consorcio tiró la toalla.

go down the drain
be wasted
irse al traste, tirarse por la borda

Years of research went down the drain when funding was cut.
Años de investigación se fueron al traste con el recorte.

bite off more than you can chew
take on more than you can manage
abarcar demasiado (quien mucho abarca, poco aprieta)

With three part-time jobs, she's bitten off more than she can chew.
Con tres trabajos a tiempo parcial, ha abarcado más de lo que puede.

a long shot
something unlikely to succeed
una posibilidad remota

It's a long shot, but we might still win the contract.
Es muy improbable, pero aún podríamos ganar el contrato.

fall flat
fail to have the intended effect
no surtir efecto, no hacer ninguna gracia

His attempt at humour fell completely flat.
Su intento de hacer gracia no tuvo ningún éxito.

burn the midnight oil
work late into the night
quemarse las pestañas

She burnt the midnight oil to finish her thesis.
Se quemó las pestañas para terminar la tesis.

go the extra mile
make more effort than is expected
ir más allá, darlo todo

Our staff always go the extra mile for clients.
Nuestro personal siempre va más allá de lo que se le pide.

explain.title: Comunicación y conflicto
head: Idiom · meaning
Español
Ejemplo · Example
rows:
beat about the bush
avoid the main point
andarse con rodeos

Stop beating about the bush and tell me what happened.
Deja de andarte con rodeos y dime qué pasó.

spill the beans
reveal a secret
irse de la lengua

Someone spilt the beans about the takeover.
Alguien se fue de la lengua sobre la adquisición.

let the cat out of the bag
reveal a secret by accident
descubrir el pastel

I let the cat out of the bag about her surprise party.
Descubrí el pastel de su fiesta sorpresa.

bite your tongue
stop yourself from saying something
morderse la lengua

I had to bite my tongue during the meeting.
Tuve que morderme la lengua en la reunión.

put your foot in it
say something tactless
meter la pata

I really put my foot in it when I mentioned his ex.
Metí la pata hasta el fondo al mencionar a su ex.

bury the hatchet
make peace after a quarrel
hacer las paces, enterrar el hacha de guerra

The two ministers have finally buried the hatchet.
Los dos ministros por fin han hecho las paces.

a bone of contention
a subject of disagreement
la manzana de la discordia

The budget remains a bone of contention.
El presupuesto sigue siendo la manzana de la discordia.

the elephant in the room
an obvious problem nobody mentions
el tema incómodo que todos evitan

Climate change was the elephant in the room at the summit.
El cambio climático era el tema que nadie quería tocar en la cumbre.

get on someone's nerves
irritate someone
sacar de quicio, poner de los nervios

His constant interruptions get on my nerves.
Sus constantes interrupciones me sacan de quicio.

explain.title: Emociones y relaciones
head: Idiom · meaning
Español
Ejemplo · Example
rows:
over the moon
extremely pleased
loco de contento, en el séptimo cielo

She was over the moon about the scholarship.
Estaba loca de contenta con la beca.

down in the dumps
sad, low
de bajón, con la moral por los suelos

He's been down in the dumps since the election.
Está de bajón desde las elecciones.

see eye to eye
agree
estar de acuerdo

We don't always see eye to eye on politics.
No siempre estamos de acuerdo en política.

get cold feet
become too nervous to go ahead
echarse atrás, rajarse

The buyer got cold feet at the last minute.
El comprador se echó atrás en el último momento.

have a chip on your shoulder
feel resentful about a past injustice
estar resentido, tener complejo

He has a chip on his shoulder about not going to university.
Está resentido por no haber ido a la universidad.

not your cup of tea
not something you like
no ser lo tuyo

Opera isn't really my cup of tea.
La ópera no es lo mío.

keep someone at arm's length
avoid becoming close to someone
mantener a alguien a distancia

She keeps journalists at arm's length.
Mantiene a los periodistas a distancia.

be head over heels (in love)
be completely in love
estar perdidamente enamorado

They're head over heels in love.
Están perdidamente enamorados.

explain.title: Decisiones, riesgo y tiempo
head: Idiom · meaning
Español
Ejemplo · Example
rows:
sit on the fence
avoid taking sides
no mojarse, nadar entre dos aguas

The senator is still sitting on the fence over the bill.
El senador sigue sin mojarse sobre el proyecto de ley.

take the plunge
finally do something risky
lanzarse a la piscina, dar el paso

After years of renting, they took the plunge and bought a flat.
Tras años de alquiler, dieron el paso y compraron un piso.

play it by ear
decide as things happen
improvisar sobre la marcha

I don't know how long the talks will last, so let's play it by ear.
No sé cuánto durarán las negociaciones, así que ya iremos viendo.

jump the gun
act too soon
precipitarse, adelantarse

The newspaper jumped the gun by announcing the result.
El periódico se precipitó al anunciar el resultado.

a blessing in disguise
something bad that turns out to be good
no hay mal que por bien no venga

Losing that job was a blessing in disguise.
Perder aquel trabajo fue, al final, una suerte.

the ball is in your court
it is your turn to act or decide
la pelota está en tu tejado

We've made our offer; the ball is in their court now.
Hemos hecho nuestra oferta; ahora la pelota está en su tejado.

cross that bridge when you come to it
deal with a problem only if it arises
no adelantar acontecimientos

What if they say no? We'll cross that bridge when we come to it.
¿Y si dicen que no? No adelantemos acontecimientos.

once in a blue moon
very rarely
de Pascuas a Ramos

My brother phones once in a blue moon.
Mi hermano llama de Pascuas a Ramos.

in the nick of time
just in time
justo a tiempo, por los pelos

The firefighters arrived in the nick of time.
Los bomberos llegaron justo a tiempo.

at the eleventh hour
at the last possible moment
en el último momento, a última hora

A deal was struck at the eleventh hour.

explain.title: Saber, entender y meterse en líos
head: Idiom · meaning
Español
Ejemplo · Example
rows:
know something inside out
know something thoroughly
conocer algo al dedillo

She knows the tax code inside out.
Se conoce el código tributario al dedillo.

ring a bell
sound familiar
sonar (de algo)

Does the name Hargreaves ring a bell?
¿Te suena el nombre de Hargreaves?

it's all Greek to me
I can't understand it at all
me suena a chino

Quantum physics? It's all Greek to me.
¿Física cuántica? Me suena a chino.

the tip of the iceberg
a small visible part of a bigger problem
la punta del iceberg

These complaints are just the tip of the iceberg.
Estas quejas son solo la punta del iceberg.

be in hot water
be in trouble
estar metido en un lío

The minister is in hot water over his expenses.
El ministro está metido en un lío por sus gastos.

a storm in a teacup
a lot of fuss about something unimportant
una tormenta en un vaso de agua

The row over the logo was a storm in a teacup.
La polémica del logo fue una tormenta en un vaso de agua.

between a rock and a hard place
facing two equally bad options
entre la espada y la pared

The government is between a rock and a hard place.
El Gobierno está entre la espada y la pared.

the last straw
the final problem that makes things unbearable
la gota que colma el vaso

The latest delay was the last straw for passengers.
El último retraso fue la gota que colmó el vaso para los pasajeros.

face the music
accept the consequences of your actions
dar la cara, afrontar las consecuencias

explain.note: Pull someone's leg = engañar a alguien en broma; take the mickey (out of someone) = burlarse de alguien (muy británico y coloquial). Algunos idioms coinciden casi palabra por palabra (the tip of the iceberg, read between the lines), pero son la excepción, no la regla.
explain.note_en: Pull someone's leg = tease someone with a false story; take the mickey = mock someone (very British, informal). Word-for-word equivalents exist, but they are the exception.

items.es: Tendremos que apretarnos el cinturón hasta que se firme el nuevo contrato.

items.en: After years of rivalry, the two families have buried the hatchet.
items.es: Tras años de rivalidad, las dos familias han hecho las paces.

items.en: Nobody dared to mention the elephant in the room: the chief executive's salary.
items.es: Nadie se atrevió a mencionar el tema incómodo: el sueldo del consejero delegado.

items.en: Winning the league is a long shot for a club like ours.
items.es: Ganar la liga es muy improbable para un club como el nuestro.

items.en: She's been down in the dumps since her dog died.
items.es: Está de bajón desde que se le murió el perro.

items.en: Heavy metal is not my cup of tea, I'm afraid.
items.es: Me temo que el heavy metal no es lo mío.

items.en: After years of hesitation, he took the plunge and moved to Dublin.
items.es: Tras años de dudas, se lanzó a la piscina y se mudó a Dublín.

items.en: His face rings a bell, but I can't remember his name.
items.es: Su cara me suena, pero no recuerdo cómo se llama.

items.en: After twenty years in the post, she knows the system inside out.
items.es: Tras veinte años en el puesto, conoce el sistema al dedillo.

items.en: The row about the new logo is just a storm in a teacup.
items.es: La polémica del nuevo logo no es más que una tormenta en un vaso de agua.

items.en: Sooner or later, the bankers will have to face the music.
items.es: Tarde o temprano, los banqueros tendrán que dar la cara.

items.en: We're all in the same boat, so let's stop complaining.
items.es: Estamos todos en el mismo barco, así que dejemos de quejarnos.

items.en: We only see our cousins once in a blue moon.
items.es: Solo vemos a nuestros primos de Pascuas a Ramos.

items.en: His constant interruptions really get on my nerves.
items.es: Sus constantes interrupciones me sacan de quicio.

items.en: With two jobs and a baby, I've bitten off more than I can chew.
items.es: Con dos trabajos y un bebé, he abarcado más de lo que puedo.

items.en: Come on, spill the beans: who got the job?
items.es: Venga, desembucha: ¿a quién le han dado el puesto?

items.en: Sorry, I had my head in the clouds. Could you repeat the question?
items.es: Perdona, estaba en las nubes. ¿Puedes repetir la pregunta?

items.en: I always have butterflies in my stomach before a job interview.
items.es: Siempre tengo un nudo en el estómago antes de una entrevista de trabajo.

items.en: Cycling to work kills two birds with one stone: I save money and keep fit.
items.es: Ir en bici al trabajo es matar dos pájaros de un tiro: ahorro dinero y me mantengo en forma.

items.en: Investors were warned not to jump the gun before the figures were published.
items.es: Se advirtió a los inversores de que no se precipitaran antes de que se publicaran las cifras.

items.en: He's got a chip on his shoulder about his accent, although nobody else notices it.
items.es: Tiene complejo con su acento, aunque nadie más se da cuenta.

items.bad: The renovation cost us an eye of the face.
items.good: The renovation cost us an arm and a leg.
items.why: Calco de «un ojo de la cara»: en inglés se paga con un brazo y una pierna.
items.why_en: Literal calque; the English image is an arm and a leg.

items.bad: After the third rejection, she threw the towel.
items.good: After the third rejection, she threw in the towel.
items.why: La partícula forma parte del bloque fijo: throw in the towel.
items.why_en: The particle in is part of the idiom.

items.bad: Sorry, I was in the clouds.
items.good: Sorry, I had my head in the clouds.
items.why: «Estar en las nubes» no se traduce literalmente; también vale I was miles away.
items.why_en: Use have your head in the clouds or be miles away.

items.bad: Quantum physics sounds Chinese to me.
items.good: Quantum physics is all Greek to me.
items.why: Cada idioma elige su lengua incomprensible: en inglés es el griego.
El número es fijo: singular. (BrE about, AmE around.)

items.bad: This plan kills two birds with one shot.
items.good: This plan kills two birds with one stone.
items.why: Casi idéntico al español… pero con piedra, no con tiro.
items.why_en: Almost the same as Spanish, but with a stone.

items.bad: I put the leg when I asked about her husband.
items.good: I put my foot in it when I asked about her husband.
items.why: «Meter la pata» → pie (foot), no pierna, y con in it.
items.why_en: The idiom is put your foot in it.

items.bad: In conclusion, the reforms went down the drain. <small>(ensayo)</small>
items.why: Registro: en un ensayo académico el idiom coloquial desentona.
items.why_en: Too colloquial for an academic essay: paraphrase.

explain.title: ¿Cómo uso un idiom sin meter la pata?

items.es: Comprueba el significado figurado y la connotación: ¿positiva, negativa, irónica?
items.en: Check the figurative meaning and its connotation.

items.es: Aprende el bloque completo, con su artículo y su partícula: throw in the towel, a piece of cake.
items.en: Learn the whole chunk, with its article and particle.

items.es: Identifica las piezas móviles: tiempo verbal, posesivo (my / your / their) y hueco de persona (someone's).
items.en: Identify the moving parts: tense, possessive, person slot.

items.es: Decide el registro: ¿conversación, columna de opinión, informe, ensayo?
items.en: Decide the register: chat, column, report or essay?

items.es: No traduzcas la imagen española: busca el equivalente funcional (un ojo de la cara → an arm and a leg).
items.en: Don't translate the Spanish image: find the functional equivalent.

items.es: Dosifica: uno o dos por párrafo como mucho. Encadenar idioms suena forzado.
items.en: One or two per paragraph at most.

lines.en: You look down in the dumps. What's up?
The client got cold feet and pulled out of the deal at the eleventh hour.
lines.es: El cliente se echó atrás y se retiró del acuerdo en el último momento.

lines.en: Oh no. So months of work have gone down the drain?
lines.es: Vaya. ¿Así que meses de trabajo se han ido al traste?

lines.en: Pretty much. And I put my foot in it by telling the boss it would be a piece of cake.
lines.es: Más o menos. Y metí la pata al decirle al jefe que sería pan comido.

lines.en: Don't throw in the towel yet. It might be a blessing in disguise.
lines.es: No tires la toalla todavía. A lo mejor no hay mal que por bien no venga.

lines.en: I doubt it. Winning a new client this quarter is a long shot.
lines.es: Lo dudo. Conseguir un cliente nuevo este trimestre es muy improbable.

lines.en: Well, I'll go the extra mile to help. We're in the same boat, after all.
lines.es: Bueno, haré lo que haga falta para ayudar. Al fin y al cabo, estamos en el mismo barco.

lines.en: Thanks. Should we tell the boss now, or cross that bridge when we come to it?
lines.es: Gracias. ¿Se lo decimos ya al jefe o esperamos a ver qué pasa?

lines.en: Now. If he hears it from someone else, we'll be in hot water.
lines.es: Ya. Si se entera por otra persona, nos meteremos en un lío.

lines.en: True. Time to face the music, then. But coffee first!
lines.es: Es verdad. Pues toca dar la cara. ¡Pero primero, un café!

explain.title: Truco: la prueba del titular
explain.es: Antes de usar un idiom en un texto formal, pregúntate: ¿lo vería en un titular de un periódico serio o en un informe oficial? At the eleventh hour, a bone of contention o the tip of the iceberg, sí; a piece of cake o take the mickey, no. Y dosifica: el diálogo modelo de esta sección está cargado a propósito para practicar, pero en la vida real menos es más; un texto lleno de idioms suena a libro de texto, no a nativo.
explain.en: Would you see it in a quality newspaper headline or an official report? If not, keep it for conversation. And remember: less is more.

exercises.title: ¿Qué significa de verdad?
exercises.es: ¿Verdadero (T) o falso (F)? Si es falso, piensa cuál es el significado correcto.
exercises.en: True or false? If false, think of the correct meaning.

items.q: If something is a long shot, it is very likely to succeed.
If you get cold feet, you become too nervous to go ahead.
A cash cow is a business that loses money every year.
items.why: It is a reliable source of profit.

items.q: If you see eye to eye with someone, you agree with them.
If a joke falls flat, everyone laughs at it.
When you burn the midnight oil, you work late into the night.
If a company is in the red, it is making a healthy profit.
items.why: It is losing money or in debt.

items.q: If you bite your tongue, you say exactly what you think.
items.why: You stop yourself from saying it.

items.q: A storm in a teacup is a lot of fuss about something unimportant.
If you keep someone at arm's length, you avoid becoming close to them.

exercises.title: Ordena la frase

items.a: She finally threw in the towel.

exercises.title: Transformaciones tipo Cambridge
exercises.es: Completa la segunda frase para que signifique lo mismo que la primera. Usa la palabra clave (sin cambiarla) y entre 3 y 8 palabras. La palabra clave activa un idiom.
exercises.en: Complete the second sentence so that it means the same as the first. Use the key word, unchanged, and 3–8 words.

items.q:
Please stop avoiding the issue and say what you mean.
→ I'd rather you ________ and said what you meant.
items.a: I'd rather you stopped beating about the bush and said what you meant.

items.q:
We paid a fortune for the holiday.
→ The holiday ________.
items.a: The holiday cost (us) an arm and a leg.

items.q:
It was Jane who accidentally revealed the secret about the merger.
→ The person ________ about the merger was Jane.
items.a: The person who let the cat out of the bag about the merger was Jane.

items.q:
The minister has yet to declare which side he supports.
→ The minister is ________.
items.a: The minister is (still) sitting on the fence.

items.q:
It is now up to the unions to respond to our offer.
→ The ball is now ________.
items.a: The ball is now in the unions' court.

items.q:
It is very rare for us to eat out these days.
→ We ________ these days.
items.a: We (only) eat out once in a blue moon these days.

items.q:
Nobody in the audience found his attempt at humour remotely funny.
→ His attempt at humour ________ the audience.
items.a: His attempt at humour fell (completely) flat with the audience.

items.q:
The deal was only saved at the very last moment.
→ It was not until ________ the deal was saved.
items.a: It was not until the eleventh hour that the deal was saved.

exercises.title: Del idiom al registro formal
exercises.es: Estas frases van a un informe oficial. Sustituye el idiom (en negrita) por una expresión neutra o formal.
exercises.en: These sentences are for an official report. Replace the idiom in bold with neutral or formal wording.

items.q: The firm has been in the red for two years.
items.a: The firm has been operating at a loss (or making a loss) for two years.

items.q: The negotiators threw in the towel after six hours.
items.a: The negotiators abandoned their efforts (or conceded defeat) after six hours.

items.q: Funding remains a bone of contention between the two departments.
items.a: Funding remains a source of disagreement (or a contentious issue) between the two departments.

items.q: The council jumped the gun by approving the plan.
items.a: The council acted prematurely in approving the plan.

items.q: Many households are struggling to make ends meet.
items.a: Many households are struggling to cover their basic living costs.

items.q: The report hits the nail on the head.
items.a: The report identifies the problem precisely (or is entirely accurate).

items.q: The opposition leader is sitting on the fence over the issue.
items.a: The opposition leader is remaining neutral (or has not taken a clear position) on the issue.

items.q: The minister is in hot water over his expenses.
items.a: The minister is facing serious criticism (or is under scrutiny) over his expenses.

exercises.title: Lee y contesta
exercises.es: Lee el artículo. Marca T (verdadero) o F (falso) y contesta las preguntas con tus propias palabras.
exercises.en: Read the article. Tick T or F and answer the questions in your own words.
text: When Marta Ruiz left her job at a Madrid bank to launch a food-delivery app, her friends thought she had bitten off more than she could chew. She had no experience in technology, and for the first eighteen months the company was firmly in the red. To make ends meet, she gave Spanish lessons in the evenings; at night, she burnt the midnight oil coding the prototype herself.

The low point came when her main investor got cold feet and withdrew, just weeks before the launch. ‘I was between a rock and a hard place,’ she recalls. ‘I could either throw in the towel or sell my flat to keep going.’ She took the plunge and sold it, although her parents, she admits, did not see eye to eye with her on that decision.

In the end, losing the investor proved a blessing in disguise. A larger fund, impressed by her determination, stepped in at the eleventh hour. Today the app is the group's cash cow, and Ruiz is understandably over the moon. Her advice to young entrepreneurs? ‘Learn the ropes before you start, and don't expect it to be a piece of cake.’

items.q: Marta's friends thought her plan was too ambitious for her.
items.why: They thought she had bitten off more than she could chew.

items.q: The company made a profit from the very beginning.
items.why: For eighteen months it was in the red.

items.q: Her main investor withdrew because he became nervous.
Marta's parents fully supported the sale of her flat.
items.why: They did not see eye to eye with her.

items.q: How did Marta make ends meet during the first eighteen months?
items.a: She gave Spanish lessons in the evenings.

items.q: What were the two options when she was ‘between a rock and a hard place’?
items.a: Giving up (throwing in the towel) or selling her flat to keep going.

items.q: Why did losing the investor turn out to be ‘a blessing in disguise’?
items.a: Because a larger fund, impressed by her determination, invested at the last moment.

items.q: Find an idiom in paragraph 3 meaning ‘a reliable source of profit’.
items.a: a cash cow

items.q: Rewrite ‘stepped in at the eleventh hour’ in neutral language.
items.a: intervened at the last possible moment

exercises.en: Translate using an English idiom. Find the equivalent, not the literal image.

items.a: That car cost them an arm and a leg.

items.q: Deja de andarte con rodeos y dime la verdad.
items.a: Stop beating about the bush and tell me the truth.

items.q: Tras el tercer rechazo, ella tiró la toalla.
items.a: After the third rejection, she threw in the towel.

items.q: La subida de precios fue la gota que colmó el vaso.
a: The price rise was the last straw.
The price increase was the last straw.

items.q: ¿Me estás tomando el pelo?

items.q: Metí la pata al preguntarle por su exmujer.

exercises.title: Ahora escribe tú
exercises.es: Escribe en inglés. Cuida la forma exacta del idiom y el registro.
exercises.en: Write in English. Watch the exact form of each idiom and the register.

items.q: Cuenta una ocasión en la que metiste la pata (put your foot in it). 2 frases.
items.a: Ej.: At a dinner party I asked our host when the baby was due. I really put my foot in it: she wasn't pregnant.

items.q: Escribe un titular de prensa con at the eleventh hour o in hot water.
items.a: Ej.: Strike averted at the eleventh hour as unions accept new pay offer.

items.q: Aconseja a alguien que quiere dejar la carrera. Usa throw in the towel y a blessing in disguise.
items.a: Ej.: Don't throw in the towel just because you failed one exam. It may turn out to be a blessing in disguise.

items.q: Dos frases sobre tu trabajo o tus estudios: una con learn the ropes y otra con pull your weight.
items.a: Ej.: It took me a month to learn the ropes. Now everyone expects me to pull my weight.

items.q: Reescribe este mensaje en tono formal: «We're in hot water: the budget's gone down the drain and the client's getting cold feet.»
items.a: Ej.: We are currently facing serious difficulties: the budget has been exhausted and the client is reconsidering their commitment.

checklist.es: Reconozco al menos 50 idioms frecuentes y sé qué significan.
checklist.en: I recognise at least 50 common idioms and know what they mean.

checklist.es: Sé qué partes de un idiom cambian (verbo, posesivo) y cuáles son fijas.
checklist.en: I know which parts of an idiom change and which are fixed.

checklist.es: Evito los calcos: cost an arm and a leg, nunca an eye of the face.
checklist.en: I avoid literal calques from Spanish.

checklist.es: Distingo los idioms coloquiales de los neutros que acepta la prensa seria.
checklist.en: I can tell colloquial idioms from neutral ones.

checklist.es: En un texto académico sustituyo un idiom coloquial por una paráfrasis formal.
checklist.en: I can paraphrase idioms in formal writing.

checklist.es: Resuelvo transformaciones tipo Cambridge C2 en las que la palabra clave activa un idiom.
checklist.en: I can do C2 key word transformations with idioms.
